source_title: Travis Perkins Annual Report and Accounts 2019
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 71 and 134 state that the strategic report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 2 March 2020; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 3.2% to £6,956m, like-for-like sales rose 3.8%, adjusted operating profit increased 7.8% to £442m and free cash flow improved to £195m. Covenant net debt rose to £344m and leverage to 2.7x, above the 2.5x target, reflecting Brexit inventory and acquisitions; excluding those items, underlying debt improved by approximately £45m. Statutory operating profit also recovered strongly.
already_announced_exclusion: The announced Wickes demerger, P&H divestment and transformation, wholesale disposal, ERP programme halt and above-branch cost reductions disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: A challenging market and leverage modestly above target create some pressure, but revenue and profit growth, stronger free cash flow and improving underlying debt provide very strong contrary evidence.

source_title: Travis Perkins Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 77 and 122 state that the strategic report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 28 February 2022; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 24% to £4,587m, like-for-like sales increased 25.4%, adjusted operating profit rose to £353m from £128m, profit after tax reached £241m after a prior-year loss and return on capital employed improved to 14.1%. Covenant net debt was £87m versus £40m, but remained low after shareholder distributions and investment, while the Group completed its strategic portfolio refocus.
already_announced_exclusion: The completed Wickes demerger, P&H sale, Merchanting cost restructuring and other portfolio-refocus actions disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: The scale of the revenue, profit and return-on-capital recovery provides exceptionally strong contrary evidence. Product availability and inflation risks and modestly higher net debt create only limited pressure.

source_title: Travis Perkins Annual Report and Accounts 2023 financial statements
availability_evidence: Annual report financial statements pages 10 and 55 state that the statements were approved by the Board on 11 March 2024; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue fell 2.7% to £4,861.9m and like-for-like sales declined 3.1%. Adjusted operating profit fell 39% to £180.4m, adjusted margin contracted to 3.7% from 5.9% and statutory profit fell to £38.1m from £192.2m. Adjusting items included £16.8m of restructuring costs, £10.1m for Benchmarx closures and a £33.1m Toolstation France impairment. Cash fell to £131.5m from £235.7m, although reported borrowings also reduced.
already_announced_exclusion: The central-functions, regional sales/support and supply-chain restructuring, £35m annualised savings, Benchmarx branch closures, Toolstation France impairment and actions, and historical Wickes and P&H portfolio actions disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Severe profit and margin deterioration, weak demand, material adjusting charges and lower cash create high pressure. Continued profitability and reduced borrowings provide only partial contrary evidence.
